While technically you are correct that editors do have some censorship powers, it is massively constrained for technical standards because the rules for validity are so clear cut. Informational EIPs necessarily require that power to be greatly expanded. No need to have a block number for Berlin yet <@!187490121698770945> from an Eth2 perspective, it would have been nice to get Berlin in before the Phase 0 launch but I understand that everything needs time. so, from the link above, what prevents Ethereum to release the implemented EIPs? Client integration -> fuzz testing -> testnet -> mainnet For BLS it is fuzz testing in particular Most of the other stuff is pretty basic Any help testing that BLS is ready for mainnet will accelerate the Berlin timeline We are closer to Berlin then it looks tbh <@!557201004060213248> is that because it would be ideal to have BLS on eth1 when eth2 launches? yes, the deposit contract should be able to reject invalid signatures. I fear we will burn a lot of ether otherwise could you briefly elaborate? (not familiar with how the deposit contract works) Well, the contract is very limited what can be checked within the EVM: ``` // Extended ABI length checks since dynamic types are used. require(pubkey.length == 48, "DepositContract: invalid pubkey length"); require(withdrawal_credentials.length == 32, "DepositContract: invalid withdrawal_credentials length"); require(signature.length == 96, "DepositContract: invalid signature length"); // Check deposit amount require(msg.value >= 1 ether, "DepositContract: deposit value too low"); require(msg.value % 1 gwei == 0, "DepositContract: deposit value not multiple of gwei"); uint deposit_amount = msg.value / 1 gwei; require(deposit_amount <= type(uint64).max, "DepositContract: deposit value too high"); ``` So, it basically does sanity checks: 1. lenght checks on the input data 2. value checks on the deposit amounts 3. further check on deposit data roots On the testnets we often had invalid deposits. That was caused by either outdated or misconfigured tooling. An invalid deposit is a deposit that _went through_ the checks in the contract but still contains an invalid BLS signature. I created a tracking ticket https://github.com/ethereum/eth2.0-specs/issues/2081 On the testnets we basically just used it to investigate why there would be invalid signatures, identified the issue and fixed the tooling. This is probably fine if we can ensure that all our tooling is battle-tested for a mainnet launch. But then again, we saw invalid deposits for _every_ testnet launch. Now that we are nearing a mainnet launch, we should tripple-check that this will not happen. Back in spring I was hoping we will get the precompile before mainnet launch, eventually allowing us to do signature checks in the contract itself, rejecting formally correct deposits with invalid signatures. That would futher prevent accidentally "burning" mainnet ether. ah i see, thank you for all the details <@!557201004060213248> There is an update on gas prices that is drafted only at the moment https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2999 I can either push it before YoloV2 (it only requires 3 constants updates in 2537) or can postpone it Has the costing curve been validated against implementations? How about a before/after comparison? Sure there are tricks to speed things up, but unless the implementations are in the client it doesn't make sense to me.
